To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
intratumoral IL‐12‐plasmid injection is a novel therapeutic approach that holds promise for the treatment of accessible melanoma lesions.
intratumoral injection with IL‐12 encoding plasmid DNA is a promising new therapeutic tool for the treatment of accessible melanoma lesions.

(i) intratumoral injection with IL‐12‐DNA induces regression of established B16‐melano­ma tumors in C57B6 mice, (ii) IL‐12 DNA‐induced tumor regression in human melanoma in a nude mouse model is mediated in part by NK cells, (iii) IL‐12‐treatment induces an antivascular effect, as shown by histological examination of treated tumors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new therapeutic approaches for the treatment of melanoma, which is the most aggressive and most lethal form of skin cancer.
the development of a new approach to cancer therapy.
the use of DNA coding for cytokines to induce a therapeutic antitumor response in mice bearing B16 melanoma or human melanoma.
